engineer noun

also engineers, engineering, mechanical engineer, civil engineer, machinist, computer engineer

classical

Liv. 24.34.2: inventor ac māchinātor bellicōrum tormentōrum, of Archimedes (Lewis & Short)
Sen. Ep. 88.22 (M-O s.v. mechanic: engineer)

Traupman 166, 167, 310
M-O s.v. mechanic: engineer
Traupman 310

māchinātor, māchinātōris m.

noun, third declension

an engineer, a builder of machines

A woman is māchinātrīx (Traupman 166). The word also means a contriver or schemer, often of crimes (hōrum omnium scelerum improbissimus māchinātor, Cic. Cat. 3.6), so the setting should make the trade clear.

Other words

  • architectus, architectī m. — a master builder, an architect

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 3.3.45: fabrī architectīque; Cic. de Or. 1.62 (Lewis & Short)

    For the engineer who designs and oversees buildings, roads and bridges; also, figuratively, the author of a plan (Lewis & Short). See architect.

  • māchinālis scientia, māchinālis scientiae f. — engineering

    also used · classical · Plin. NH 7.125 (Lewis & Short, s.v. māchinālis); Traupman 166, 310

    Pliny’s phrase for the knowledge of machines, of Archimedes (NH 7.125); Traupman gives it for engineering. Gellius has disciplīna mēchanica (see technology).

Examples

  • inventor ac māchinātor bellicōrum tormentōrum

    the inventor and builder of engines of warLiv. 24.34.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • magistrī et māchinātōrēs, quibus ingenium et audācia erat

    the master builders and engineers, who had the talent and the daringTac. Ann. 15.42 (Lewis & Short)

  • māchinātor (māchinātrīx) computātrālis

    a computer engineerTraupman 295

See also mechanic, technology, machine, architect.
